report.summary: Host WS-ENG-21 exhibited suspicious malware execution behavior: an unauthorized executable (updsvc.exe) ran from a user AppData Temp directory, generated a burst of DGA-like high-entropy DNS queries with multiple NXDOMAIN responses, and established external HTTPS connections to 198.51.100.77:443.

claims.text: The alerting tool reported a burst of failed DNS lookups for unregistered domains from host WS-ENG-21.
Host WS-ENG-21 recorded 2 process events, 3 network connections, and 9 DNS queries between 2026-11-10T14:00:00+00:00 and 2026-11-10T14:00:55+00:00.
Process PID 9100 running C:\Users\kim\AppData\Local\Temp\updsvc.exe was spawned by explorer.exe (PID 2000) under user CORP\kim.
Updsvc.exe established 3 outbound network connections to external destination 198.51.100.77:443.
DNS query logs showed a burst of lookups with long, random-looking labels exhibiting high character entropy, including 8 lookups returning no address.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-ENG-21 from the network to prevent further C2 communications and potential lateral movement.
Terminate process PID 9100 (updsvc.exe) and remove the binary from C:\Users\kim\AppData\Local\Temp\.
Collect forensic artifacts and memory dumps from WS-ENG-21 for deeper analysis.
Block external IP address 198.51.100.77 and the associated DGA domains at the perimeter firewall and DNS sinkhole.
Tune detection rules for suspicious user-writable temporary directory process executions and high-entropy DNS query bursts.
